title: Molecular dynamics and evolutionary conservation of FUL-SOC1 regulatory interactions in polyploid Brassica juncea.
authors: Kaur, Simran; Sisodia, Rinki; Pareek, Mohit; Sri, Tanu; Chattopadhyay, Swetannita; Yaduvanshi, Priya; Asthana, Shailendra; Madhurantakam, Chaithanya; Singh, Anandita
one_liner_zh: 该文结合分子动力学模拟与进化保守性分析，研究多倍体芥菜中FUL蛋白与SOC1启动子（TF-DNA）的结合动态与补偿性突变机制，属TF-DNA互作建模，但以植物农艺性状应用为主，深度有限。
abstract: Binding of FUL with SOC1 promoter is necessary for promoting floral transition. Structural insights on mechanisms of binding can be exploited to modify DNA-protein interactions. In polyploid Brassicas, naturally diverse homologs of FUL proteins and SOC1 promoters likely regulate flowering time by way of complex interactions patterns. The dynamics of these, however, remain unexplored. Herein, we report natural structural variation among 51 FUL homologs from 25 Brassicaceae species and 3 BjuSOC1promoter homeologs. The 5'-distal deletions of BjuSOC1promoters with diverse TFBS profiles, exhibited differential GUS activity. Genetic complementation of soc1-2 mutant with BjupSOC1: AtSOC1 constructs revealed differential strength of promoter homeologs, manifesting as variable potential of flowering and AtSOC1 levels. Despite structural variation, docked FUL:pSOC1 complexes, depicted similar binding affinity stabilized by both conserved and unique residues. Molecular dynamics simulations highlighted impact of mutations on interactions. Root Mean Square Deviation revealed conformational flexibility of docked FUL: pSOC1 complexes, while Root Mean Square Fluctuation values demonstrated structural flexibility of FUL proteins bound to SOC1 promoters. The MM-GBSA-based binding free energy parameters and interaction mapping showed that mutations in FUL proteins and SOC1 promoters are compensatory permitting conservation of interaction potential. Yeast one-hybrid assays validated in silico interaction patterns. This study is essential since interacting amino-acid and nucleotide residues can be modified to design novel alleles of FUL and SOC1 with enhanced binding potential to achieve early flowering, a key agronomic trait.
abstract_zh: FUL与SOC1启动子的结合对于促进开花转变是必需的。关于结合机制的结构性见解可用于修饰DNA-蛋白质相互作用。在多倍体芸薹属植物中，FUL蛋白和SOC1启动子的自然多样化同源物可能通过复杂的相互作用模式调控开花时间。然而，这些动态变化尚未被探索。在此，我们报告了来自25个十字花科物种的51个FUL同源物和3个BjuSOC1启动子同源物的自然结构变异。具有不同TFBS谱的BjuSOC1启动子5‘-远端缺失表现出差异性的GUS活性。用BjupSOC1: AtSOC1构建体对soc1-2突变体进行遗传互补，揭示了启动子同源物的差异性强度，表现为开花潜力和AtSOC1水平的可变性。尽管存在结构变异，对接的FUL:pSOC1复合物显示出相似的结合亲和力，由保守和独特残基共同稳定。分子动力学模拟突出了突变对相互作用的影响。均方根偏差揭示了对接FUL: pSOC1复合物的构象灵活性，而均方根波动值则展示了与SOC1启动子结合的FUL蛋白的结构灵活性。基于MM-GBSA的结合自由能参数和相互作用图谱显示，FUL蛋白和SOC1启动子中的突变是补偿性的，允许相互作用潜力的保守。酵母单杂交实验验证了计算机模拟的相互作用模式。这项研究至关重要，因为相互作用的氨基酸和核苷酸残基可以被修饰，以设计具有增强结合潜力的FUL和SOC1新等位基因，从而实现早花，这是一个关键的农艺性状。
